sections.heading: Feasibility experiment: can the control panel adapt to a system it didn't create?
sections.text:
This is a proposal. Nothing has been run yet.

The question: can one adapter, mostly through configuration, read an existing design system? And can it support the core loop on that system: inspect → suggest → propose an edit → see the impact → PR + Figma change set?

sections.heading: Stage 0: our own three systems (cheapest, most honest)
sections.text:
- Inputs:
  - DSN: 431 DTCG tokens, React.
  - Starter Pack: non-DTCG export, Base UI.
  - ASSA kit: DTCG-style tokens with modes inside $value, custom elements. Only the tokens; the components are out of scope.
- Why first: three grammars, two token models (tiers vs modes) and two Figma files we control. If the contract can't describe these, stop before touching a client.
- Test: write contract v0 by hand for each, then see what an adapter can fill automatically.

sections.heading: Stage 1: one simple public design system
sections.text:
Selection criteria (all must hold):
1. React components in a public repo with a permissive licence.
2. Tokens in JSON (DTCG, Style Dictionary or similar).
3. A public Figma community file with variables, ideally matching the code release.
4. Small enough to inspect by hand: roughly 20–60 components.
5. Storybook present (lets us test reading the Storybook manifest).
6. Not built on our stack, so it isn't a disguised greenfield.

Candidates to verify against the criteria (none checked yet):
- Workday Canvas Kit
- GitHub Primer (React + Primitives; may be too large)
- Twilio Paste

If none has drift, we create it on purpose. Duplicate the community Figma file into a sandbox and change 10 known items: renamed variables, an unbound fill, a variant missing in code. That gives a ground truth for precision.

sections.heading: What to test
sections.text:
# · Step · Pass looks like · Fail looks like

1 · Read tokens into the contract · Most tokens map to roles without renaming; the rest are listed for a human decision · Needs per-token code
2 · Discover components · The panel lists the real components with props, from code or the Storybook manifest · Needs a hand-written list
3 · Link Figma · Variables matched to code names; mismatches listed · No reliable match without renaming Figma
4 · Drift scan · Findings on a manually checked sample are mostly correct; seeded items found · Many false positives, or seeded items missed
5 · Suggestion · At least 3 rule-based suggestions that a DS lead agrees are worth doing · Generic or wrong advice
6 · Propose an edit · One token edit produces a branch + PR with an impact list · Edit can't be expressed in their file format
7 · Figma change set · The plugin's 3-way review shows the same change and applies it to the sandbox file · The plugin only works on starter-derived names (current behaviour, variables-model.ts L80)
8 · Adapter effort · Log hours and what had to be coded vs configured · Not measured as a target; we record it

sections.heading: Decision rule
sections.text:
- All of 1–7 pass with config only: Path B becomes a product module; book a pilot client.
- 1–4 pass, 6–7 need code: the panel is read-only for brownfield; edits stay a service.
- 1–3 fail: Path B stays a service with scripts; the MVP is Path A only, plus the assessment as a service.

sections.heading: Who and what
sections.text:
- One practice member running it, one reviewer from the other two.
- Read-only on the public repo (a fork or local clone). A sandbox copy of the Figma file. Never a client file.

sections.heading: What not to claim afterwards
sections.text: Even a full pass proves one profile: React + JSON tokens + Figma variables. It does not prove "any design system".
